questions.question: What is the default width behavior of a block-level element in HTML?
options: It takes only as much width as its text content requires
It automatically spans 100% of the available width of its parent container
It has a fixed width of 800 pixels
It collapses to zero width unless specified in CSS
questions.hint: Block elements stretch to fill the horizontal line.
questions.explanation: A block element expands to fill the entire horizontal width of its container.

questions.question: How do pure inline elements respond to CSS width and height properties?
options: They ignore width and height properties entirely
They throw a CSS parser error
questions.hint: Dimensions only apply to block and inline-block.

questions.question: Which CSS display value combines inline flow with configurable width and height dimensions?
questions.explanation: display: inline-block allows elements to flow horizontally like text while respecting width, height, and vertical margins.
